thread:
maria g: Quick follow-up to the transport/pagination RFC — thought about making timeouts and retry policies configurable per-connector. proposal: explicit per-page retry budget + per-request timeouts. open to bikeshedding.

alex r: +1 to explicit budgets. question: can we do this without changing the main call surface for simple use?

cheng li: If it's hidden, folks won't tune it. my vote: opt-in advanced config object, e.g. `TransportConfig { connect_timeout, request_timeout, retry_policy, page_retry_window_ms }`. keeps defaults stable.

samir: Go prefers functional options: `NewClient(opts ...Option)`. avoids passing structs everywhere. we can provide a `WithTransportConfig(tc)` option.

olivia p: One semantics question: does `page_retry_window` apply to each page fetch attempt or to the whole iteration across pages? that changes UX a lot.

maria g: proposal: page_retry_window applies per-page fetch (so each page has its own retry budget). if a page exhausts its budget, iterator returns an error and we allow callers to resume via a continuation cursor. default `auto_paginate: true`.

cheng li: server-side note: this relies on stable continuation tokens for resume. we already have mostly stable tokens but will add stronger guarantees in docs and tests.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary: sdk-transport-config-staging deployed to staging (build #4125) :rocket:

alex r: to minimize breakage: export a global `defaultTransportConfig` at SDK root and a per-client `client.withTransportConfig(...)` so existing calls continue to work.

samir: Go-specific: iterator should return `PageResult{Items, NextCursor, Err}` instead of closing channels or panicking when a page fails. that makes resume explicit.

olivia p: also recommend default retry/backoff: jittered-exponential with max_attempts=4 and per-page budget default 2000ms, with easy override in `TransportConfig`. will write a short doc blurb.

maria g: ok i'll draft a follow-up RFC PR with the config shapes for Python/TS/Go + migration notes, breaking changes (none by default), and examples. who wants to own the Go shape + tests?

samir: I'll take the Go shape + unit/integration tests.

alex r: i'll prototype TS ergonomics and a tiny ergonomic shim for `client.withTransportConfig`.

cheng li: i'll update server docs about token stability and add an e2e test.

maria g: thanks everyone. i'll spin the PR and tag owners in it. moving this to RFC follow-up. :pray: 

alex r: :thumbsup:

olivia p: fwiw, we should also surface an example for 'paginated search with aggressive retries' in the docs site.

maria g: good call — will add an example snippet in the PR.

samir: quick note for release: bump SDK minor, release notes should highlight `TransportConfig` opt-in only.

maria g: noted. closing thread for now, ping in the PR for follow-ups.
